ratings_why.fun: Every turn asks a clear question, bank the Heat now or keep heating towards a better rate, and one hot piece growing into a masterpiece is a satisfying arc to watch.
ratings_why.distinct: Attack-only Heat that you harden by Quenching, plus melting sold units into your carry, plays unlike any of today's tribes, though the counter-on-units core is familiar.

verdict_why: v2 cleaned up the wording that was unclear; what is left are small phrasing tweaks and taste, not fixes.

points.text: Heat and Quench read as smithing at a glance: heat the metal, quench to harden, melt down scrap. The forge fantasy comes through in what the cards do, not just in their names.
Brother Paracel says 'half its Heat'; 'half of that unit's own Heat' would remove the brief doubt about whether it means Paracel's Heat.
The salamander half of the seed is thin: only Ottilie's regrowth and the Wet Cellar show it. A warning-colour or toxic-skin card, such as Heat that burns attackers, would let it show in play.
Bellows Boy now reads as two rules in one line. 'End of Turn: the units on the other row next to this gain 1 Heat' says the same thing more simply.
Smooth Tobias' text (gets hotter when hit) doesn't show his regrown-tail joke; a small regrow effect would suit the name better.

standouts.why: Ottilie is regrowth paid for in Heat: one line, instantly readable, and the most salamander card in the tribe.
Grandmaster's '10 or more' threshold at +3/+3 makes the bank-or-wait choice concrete and easy to read.
Crucible Keeper melts what you sell into your carry: the 'buy fewer bodies' plan in one simple trigger.

weakest.why: Old Cinderheart is a plain multiplier with no forge flavour in its text and little effect on its own.
Bellows Boy changes which way it works by row, which is more to read than such a plain card should ask.
Guild Assayer is clear but generic: free Heat with no decision attached.

flags.note: Golden Nutrisco leaves all the Heat, so the Grandmaster Quenches the same 10+ Heat for +30/+30 every turn while the Heat keeps rising.
Konrad returning a Quench-Bucket Runner every turn gives a fresh Quench and 3 Heat each turn; worth a look in sims.
